stages.title: Public goods
stages.sub: Why the free market fails to provide public goods at all.

steps.q: A street light shines for one passer-by. Does that use up light for the next person who walks by?
steps.right: No, there is just as much light left for them
steps.wrong: Yes, there is less light left for them
steps.hint: Think about whether one person looking at the light stops another person seeing it too.

steps.q: A council puts up a street light on a public road. Can it stop someone who won't pay council tax from benefiting?
steps.right: No, anyone walking past benefits either way
steps.wrong: Yes, it can block non-payers from the light
steps.hint: Is there a gate or meter that only lets paying people see the light?

steps.q: An ice cream is used up, and the shop can withhold it until you pay. Does a street light share both features?
steps.right: No, the street light lacks both features
steps.wrong: Yes, the street light works the same way
steps.hint: Think back to what you found for the light: could use be limited, and could non-payers be blocked?

steps.q: Nobody can be stopped from enjoying the street light, paying or not. Would a rational person pay towards it, or wait for others?
steps.right: Wait and let others pay for it

steps.q: If a private firm knows almost nobody will pay for the street lights it builds, will it have any reason to build them?
steps.right: No, it will provide little or none
steps.wrong: Yes, it will still build plenty
steps.hint: Would a firm keep supplying something it cannot get paid for?
